original_value: We study response generation for open domain conversation in chatbots. Existing methods assume that words in responses are generated from an identical vocabulary regardless of their inputs, which not only makes them vulnerable to generic patterns and irrelevant noise, but also causes a high cost in decoding. We propose a dynamic vocabulary sequence-to-sequence (DVS2S) model which allows each input to possess their own vocabulary in decoding. In training, vocabulary construction and response generation are jointly learned by maximizing a lower bound of the true objective with a Monte Carlo sampling method. In inference, the model dynamically allocates a small vocabulary for an input with the word prediction model, and conducts decoding only with the small vocabulary.  Because of the dynamic vocabulary mechanism, DVS2S eludes many generic patterns and irrelevant words in generation, and enjoys efficient decoding at the same time. Experimental results on both automatic metrics and human annotations show that DVS2S can significantly outperform state-of-the-art methods in terms of response quality, but only requires 60% decoding time compared to the most efficient baseline.

result.paraphrase: We investigate response generation for open-domain chatbot conversations. Prior methods assume that replies draw from the same vocabulary for every input, which makes them susceptible to generic phrasing and irrelevant noise while also increasing decoding cost. We introduce a dynamic vocabulary sequence-to-sequence (DVS2S) model that assigns each input its own decoding vocabulary. During training, vocabulary construction and response generation are learned jointly by maximizing a lower bound on the true objective via Monte Carlo sampling. At inference time, the model uses a word prediction module to dynamically choose a small vocabulary for each input and performs decoding only within that reduced set. Thanks to this dynamic vocabulary mechanism, DVS2S avoids many generic patterns and irrelevant words while also enabling efficient decoding. Results from both automatic metrics and human judgments indicate that DVS2S can substantially outperform state-of-the-art methods in response quality, while using only 60% of the decoding time of the most efficient baseline.
